structured_output.summary: No blocking problems. One small behaviour difference in make_conditional is untested, and the Accept-Ranges and Content-Length restore code is heavy but needed.

findings.text: make_conditional now raises 416 for an unparseable Range header before the If-Range check, whereas the old code skipped range handling when If-Range did not match, so "behaves as before" does not hold for that combination.
No test covers an invalid or non-bytes Range header together with a mismatching If-Range via make_conditional, which is the case where the new ordering differs from the old.

The save and restore of Accept-Ranges and Content-Length around apply_conditions/apply_range is verbose; it exists only to keep the old make_conditional behaviour, so a short comment saying so would help.
